mainTopic: The end of the story of the כהן גדול ישׂשכר איש כפר ברקאי: his contempt for the king, his punishment, and two אמוראים showing his answer was wrong according to the משנה and the פסוק. Then the הדרן closing פרק מקום שנהגו.
overview: This עמוד finishes a story that began on the previous עמוד. A king and queen argued over whether goat meat or lamb meat is better, and they asked the כהן גדול ישׂשכר איש כפר ברקאי to decide. He waved his hand with contempt and said lamb must be better because the תמיד is a lamb. The king ordered his right hand cut off for disrespecting the kingdom. ישׂשכר bribed the official, who cut off his left hand instead, and when the king found out he had the right hand cut off too. רב יוסף thanks ה׳ that ישׂשכר was punished in this world, measure for measure, because he used to wrap his hands in silk to avoid touching the קרבנות. רב אשי then says ישׂשכר did not know the משנה of רבי שמעון, which teaches that lambs and goats are equal. רבינא goes further and says the plain פסוק already lets a person bring either one. The עמוד ends with the הדרן closing פרק מקום שנהגו, which also completes the section called פסח ראשון.

steps.title: ישׂשכר answers the king with a rude gesture
steps.stepSummary: ישׂשכר איש כפר ברקאי waves his hand dismissively and says that if goat were better, it would be used for the תמיד.
steps.simpleTranslation: He gestured with his hand: If goat is better, let it be brought up as the daily offering!
steps.whatsHappening: The story continues from the previous עמוד. The כהן גדול answers the king's question about lamb versus goat, and he does it with a mocking hand-wave.
steps.deeperAnalysis: His argument is that the תמיד is always a lamb, so lamb must be the better meat. The point of the story, though, is how he answered. Waving his hand at a king shows that he had no respect for the monarchy, and that leads to the next step.

keyTerms.meaning: The daily offering (תמיד), which is always a lamb

steps.confusionAlert: This is not the start of a new story. The setup is on the previous עמוד: a king and queen were arguing over which meat is better, and they asked the כהן גדול to decide.

phrases.english: He signaled with his hand:
phrases.notes: It was a scornful, dismissive wave of the hand.

phrases.english: If goat is better,
let it be brought up for the daily offering.
phrases.notes: Since the תמיד is a lamb, he concludes that lamb must be better.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the story from the previous עמוד.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: ישׂשכר claims lamb is better because the תמיד uses lamb, and he shows contempt for the king while saying it.

steps.title: The king orders ישׂשכר's right hand cut off
steps.stepSummary: Because ישׂשכר showed no fear of the monarchy, the king orders his right hand cut off.
steps.simpleTranslation: The king said: Since he has no fear of the kingdom, cut off his right hand.
steps.whatsHappening: The king reacts to the disrespect, not to the answer itself, and orders a punishment.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The king's reason is stated clearly: ישׂשכר showed no awe of the kingdom. Rashi explains that the problem was not only that he disagreed, but that he answered mockingly (בלשון צחוק), with his hand-gesture. The text does not say why the hand was chosen. The idea that the punishment fit the crime comes from רב יוסף in step 4.

keyTerms.meaning: Fear or awe of the kingdom

phrases.english: The king said:
Since he does not have
fear of the kingdom,
let them cut off his right hand.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: The king's response to ישׂשכר's contemptuous answer.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: ישׂשכר's right hand is to be cut off for disrespecting the monarchy.

steps.title: A bribe backfires, and both hands are cut off
steps.stepSummary: ישׂשכר bribes the official to cut off his left hand instead. The king finds out and has the right hand cut off too.
steps.simpleTranslation: He gave a bribe, and the official cut off his left hand. The king heard about it and had his right hand cut off as well.
steps.whatsHappening: ישׂשכר tries to escape the punishment through a bribe, and it only makes things worse. He ends up losing both hands.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The bribe meant he lost his left hand, and then the king still took the right one. This sets up רב יוסף's comment in the next step that the punishment was fitting.

phrases.english: He gave a bribe, and he (the official) cut off his left hand.
The king heard, and he cut off his right hand.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Shows how the king's order was carried out and how the bribe backfired.

steps.title: רב יוסף blesses God for punishing ישׂשכר in this world
steps.stepSummary: רב יוסף says: Blessed is ה׳, Who took payment from ישׂשכר in this world.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יוסף said: Blessed is the Merciful One Who collected payment from ישׂשכר איש כפר ברקאי in this world.
steps.whatsHappening: רב יוסף comments on the story. He sees the punishment as divine justice that ישׂשכר received in this world.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Earlier in the story, ישׂשכר used to wrap his hands in silk so he would not touch the קרבנות directly, which was a disgrace to the עבודה. Losing his hands is מדה כנגד מדה, measure for measure. Being punished in this world is seen as a kindness, because it spares him a worse punishment later.

keyTerms.meaning: Who weighed out his due (collected payment)

steps.whyThisMatters: The story shows how serious it is to treat the עבודה with disrespect, and it shows the idea of מדה כנגד מדה.

phrases.english: Rav Yosef said:
Blessed is the Merciful One
Who collected from Yissachar of Kfar Barkai
his retribution from him in this world.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: A moral comment on the outcome of the story.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: ישׂשכר's punishment was fitting divine justice, delivered in this world.

steps.title: רב אשי says ישׂשכר never learned the משנה
steps.stepSummary: רב אשי says ישׂשכר איש כפר ברקאי was ignorant of a משנה that settles the question he was asked.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב אשי said: ישׂשכר איש כפר ברקאי did not learn the משנה.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא shifts from the story to the content of ישׂשכר's answer. רב אשי says his answer shows he did not know the משנה, and the proof comes in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: ישׂשכר claimed lamb is better than goat. רב אשי is preparing to show that a משנה says the two are equal, so the answer was simply wrong.

phrases.english: Rav Ashi said:
Yissachar of Kfar Barkai
did not learn the Mishnah.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from the story to a critique of ישׂשכר's answer.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: ישׂשכר's claim that lamb is better shows he was ignorant of the משנה.

steps.title: The משנה of רבי שמעון: lambs and goats are equal
steps.stepSummary: The משנה says lambs are listed before goats everywhere in the Torah, but a פסוק reverses the order to teach that the two are equal.
steps.simpleTranslation: As we learned: רבי שמעון says, lambs come before goats everywhere. You might think that is because they are the choicer species. Therefore the verse says, 'If he brings a lamb as his offering,' which teaches that both are equal.
steps.whatsHappening: This is רב אשי's proof. The משנה shows that lambs are not better than goats.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Usually the Torah mentions lambs first, which could suggest lambs are superior. But in the חטאת section, the goat appears first and the lamb comes after ("אם כבש יביא קרבנו"). That reversal teaches that the order means nothing about quality: the two animals are equal.
steps.confusionAlert: Do not misread this as saying lambs are better. The משנה brings up that idea (יכול, 'you might think') only so it can reject it. The conclusion is that the two are equal.

phrases.english: As we learned: Rabbi Shimon says:
Lambs precede goats everywhere,
one might think it is because they are choicer as a species —
therefore the verse states:
'If he brings a lamb as his offering,'
phrases.notes: This verse comes after the goat in the חטאת section, so here the order is reversed.

phrases.english: this teaches that both are equal as one.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Provides the source for רב אשי's claim.
steps.raayaObject: רב אשי's claim that ישׂשכר did not know the משנה.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The משנה of רבי שמעון that lambs and goats are equal.

steps.title: רבינא: he did not even read the verse correctly
steps.stepSummary: רבינא goes further: even the plain פסוק shows a person may bring either a lamb or a goat.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבינא said: He did not even read the Torah, for it is written 'If a lamb' and 'If a goat.' If one wants a lamb, let him bring it. If one wants a goat, let him bring it.
steps.whatsHappening: רבינא makes a stronger criticism than רב אשי. ישׂשכר did not need advanced learning to get this right, because the simple פסוק already shows the answer.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The Torah says "אם כבש" and "אם עז", giving a free choice between the two. If one were truly better, the Torah would not leave it as an open choice. So the basic מקרא already shows the two are equal.
steps.whatToRemember: Both רב אשי (from the משנה) and רבינא (from the פסוק) hold that lambs and goats are of equal value. ישׂשכר's answer was both arrogant and wrong.

phrases.english: Ravina said:
He did not even read Scripture either,
as it is written: 'If a lamb,' 'If a goat,'
if he wants a lamb — let him bring it,
if he wants a goat — let him bring it.

steps.triggerLanguage: רָבִינָא אָמַר: אֲפִילּוּ מִקְרָא נָמֵי לָא קְרָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A stronger, more basic criticism than רב אשי's.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The verses give a free choice between lamb and goat, so neither is better.

steps.title: הדרן — Closing פרק מקום שנהגו and the פסח ראשון section
steps.stepSummary: The הדרן formula closes פרק מקום שנהגו and marks the completion of the section of מסכת פסחים called פסח ראשון.
steps.simpleTranslation: We will return to you, מקום שנהגו, and פסח ראשון is concluded.
steps.whatsHappening: This is the closing formula for the end of the פרק. It is not part of the discussion itself.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Besides closing the פרק, the words "וסליקא לה פסח ראשון" note that the first part of מסכת פסחים, the part about חמץ and the laws leading up to פסח, is now finished. The next part deals with the קרבן פסח.

keyTerms.meaning: We will return to you (said at the end of a פרק)
The name of the first section of מסכת פסחים

phrases.english: We will return to you, Makom Shenahagu
and Pesach Rishon is concluded

steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: End of פרק מקום שנהגו and of the section called פסח ראשון.
